paragraphs: Children in care in Coventry live with carers approved by Coventry City Council's fostering service or by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council says children come into its care because of a crisis at home, because parents need extra support, or because of concerns such as drug or alcohol dependency or violence in the home, and that foster carers give them a safe local home while decisions about their future are made.

Coventry says it particularly needs carers who can keep brothers and sisters together, carers for teenagers, and carers for children with more complex needs. It is also looking for people to offer parent and child fostering, and for its Next Steps scheme, which needs experience of working with young people. To encourage carers to take siblings, the council pays its fee for each child placed.

The council's 2026/2027 payments leaflet sets a weekly allowance for each child from £195.67 for children aged up to 4 to £337.40 for young people aged 16 and over. Mainstream carers also receive a weekly fee per child of £175.40 at the standard level or £269.78 at the enhanced level, and five extra weeks of allowance are paid through the year for birthdays, festivals, holidays and clothing. Our Coventry allowance page has the full table.

The council runs drop-in and information events, and its fostering team is based at One Friargate in the city centre. Before choosing a service, speak to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about training, support and pay.
